messages:
rita: FYI - small batch jobs are piling up Pending in eu-west1a since ~09:40. eviction rate climbing.

 tom: saw that. dashboard shows pending_gpu_pods spiking and attach-detach queue length jumping. any scheduler rejects?

 dan: grabbed scheduler logs: repeating failures like `MatchNodeSelector` and `Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` even though node allocatable shows free GPUs. also a bunch of CNI warnings about conntrack.

 rita: snippet from scheduler: ```I0322 09:42:12.543  scheduler_predicates.go:214] Pod batch-small-12 failed predicate PodFitsHostPorts: node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeAffinity```

 nora: CNI log excerpt: ```W0322 09:41:58.102 cni.go:78] conntrack: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet```

 tom: interesting. if conntrack is full, kubelet/CNI might intermittently mark network unavailable which could cause our custom affinity predicate to treat node as ineligible.

 dan: attach-detach-controller metrics show multiple attach ops stuck 30-90s. some nodes showing attach->detach loops.

 rita: hypothesis: transient NetworkUnavailable on GPU nodes trips affinity/topology checks for gang-scheduled pods. scheduler then evicts or refuses placement, causing churn across racks.

 nora: short-term mitigations: 1) bump nf_conntrack_max on eu-west1a, 2) add a small network-ready grace to our scheduler predicate, 3) relax strict nodeAffinity for the tiny batch queue (non-prod).

 tom: ops runbook request: what's current conntrack on hosts?

 infra-bot: current nf_conntrack_max=131072 on pool eu-west1a. proposed canary bump to 524288. daemonset will apply sysctl; plan includes health checks.

 dan: I can open a tiny PR to add `--network-ready-grace=30s` to our custom predicate and gate it behind a feature flag for non-prod queues.

 rita: please do. ops, canary bump two nodes and watch pending_gpu_pods + attach queue. set alert if no improvement in 8m.

 infra-bot: canary started on nodes g-eu-a-21,g-eu-a-22. applying `/etc/sysctl.d/99-conntrack.conf` and reloading.

 tom: after canary: those nodes show conntrack_count ~12k (headroom) and pending pods scheduled onto them, attach queue cleared for jobs routed to those racks. great sign.

 nora: still seeing some cross-az reschedules: scheduler tries to place remaining pods in other AZs and bumps into capacity mismatch because of strict affinity. that caused more preemptions.

 dan: note for postmortem: eviction churn = ~1.9 GPU-hours lost in eu-west1a during spike. root cause chain: conntrack exhaustion -> transient NetworkUnavailable -> scheduler affinity predicate fails -> gang scheduling rejects -> preemption churn.

 rita: runbook snippet for on-call: ```# quick checks
ssh $NODE
sudo ss -s
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
# temporary bump
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
# persist
echo "net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288" | sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/99-conntrack.conf
sudo sysctl --system
```

 tom: longer term action items: - ensure conntrack headroom on GPU nodes via baseline sysctl limit, - add scheduler predicate grace for transient network flips, - audit small-gang job affinity rules and relax where safe.

 nora: i'll run a BQ query to count `label:small-batch` pods with nodeAffinity=true and share numbers here in 30m.

 infra-bot: canary finished: no regressions. scheduling a pool-wide roll in 45m unless someone objects.

 rita: thanks all. dan post the PR link when ready and tag me. will follow up on the audit numbers. :thumbsup:
